thread:
maria_support: FYI customer reported a spike of 503s and weird auth failures after we started spillover from eu-west -> us-east. They saw a bunch of long tails and tokens flagged as invalid when requests hit the fallback region. Logs attached below.

ashley_infra: Can you paste the customer's request ids and the exact timestamps? I want to check region capacity and queue metrics.

maria_support: Sure — sample ids: req_17ab3c, req_17ab3d, req_17ab3f. Window: 2025-09-03T14:02:10Z -> 2025-09-03T14:08:30Z. Customer says outage lasted ~6m, then recovered after their retries cleared.

jon_eng: Quick read — looks like auto-fallback kicked in due to queue depth in eu-west. When fallback happens we route to first compatible variant which can be in a different region; if the token namespace doesn't align (short-lived tokens tied to region) that can cause auth failures.

maria_support: Example log lines from our routing service:
```
[2025-09-03T14:03:12Z] route_decision: src=eu-west target=eu-west status=queued queue_len=118
[2025-09-03T14:03:14Z] route_decision: src=eu-west fallback=us-east reason=capacity_exhaustion queue_len=121
[2025-09-03T14:03:15Z] proxy: upstream=us-east auth_result=401 error=token_mismatch token_ns=eu-west
[2025-09-03T14:03:16Z] proxy: upstream=us-east respond=503 latency=1240ms
```

jon_eng: That's consistent. Two separate issues layered: (1) eu-west hit a capacity threshold and queued, triggering auto_spillover; (2) the fallback path doesn't reuse the same auth token namespace so some requests got 401 instead of being retried.

ashley_infra: I'm pulling infra metrics now — eu-west GPU pool was at 100% reserved + burst used, queueing algorithm allowed up to 125 before triggering spill. Confirmed autoscale didn't start because reserved commit reached.

maria_support: Customer asked why fallback went to us-east specifically; they expected regional pinning. They have reserved capacity but it was exhausted overnight because of a spike in eval jobs.

jon_eng: Actionable mitigation: (A) temporarily disable cross-region fallback for this customer (policy: route.policy.fallback=off for tenant acme-corp) — immediate stopgap; (B) increase eu-west reserved pool or approve burst buffer; (C) fix token namespace propagation so that fallback keeps the auth context or performs token translation.

ashley_infra: I can apply (A) now for acme-corp. Doing: `rbac update-tenant --id acme-corp --fallback disabled` — will confirm after propagation.

sre-bot: change applied by ashley_infra at 2025-09-03T14:10:01Z — propagation complete to control-plane nodes (version 2.9.1).

maria_support: Customer confirmed 5m after change they no longer saw auth failures but still saw higher tail latencies because of queue draining.

jon_eng: For longer-term: (1) change default policy so auto_spill considers auth namespace equivalence before allowing cross-region fallback; (2) tune queue thresholds to prefer rejecting early vs cross-region fallback for tenants with region-pinned tokens; (3) add a pre-fallback check that attempts token translation. I'll make an RFC.

tim_product: Can we add a console flag so customers can opt-in/out of cross-region fallback per-model or per-tenant? Product request noted.

maria_support: Filed support ticket SUP-9182 with customer communication and temporary mitigations. Also opened infra incident INF-4021 for capacity review and ENG-1234 for token propagation fix.

jon_eng: Repro steps for eng:
1) Create tenant with region pin eu-west and short-lived tokens (ttl 60s).
2) Saturate eu-west pool using load-generator (script below).
3) Observe route_decision logs and confirm fallback to us-east and 401s for some requests.

Load-generator quick script (for repro):
```
# flood eu-west until queue fills
for i in `seq 1 200`; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $SHORT_TOKEN" \
    "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rw-1.5&region=eu-west" &
done
wait
```

ashley_infra: I've scheduled a capacity bump for eu-west for today as temporary relief, and we will monitor. Also enabling tighter alerting on "queue_len > 100 && reserved_usage > 95%".

maria_support: Customer updated: appreciative of the fast response, asked for ETA on the token fix.

jon_eng: ETA for ENG-1234 (token propagation fix) is EOW sprint — I'll assign and put a canary to validate fallback auth behavior.

maria_support: Summary of next steps:
- Support: keep customer updated (maria_support)
- Infra: monitor and capacity bump (ashley_infra, INF-4021)
- Eng: token namespace propagation fix + RFC for fallback policy (jon_eng, ENG-1234)

maria_support: Closing this thread — will reopen if customer sees more regressions. :thumbsup:
